changes.id: partitioned lifecycle as the only qualified profile (governor Option 1)
files: tests updated to the partitioned profile (see delta)
changes.note: Every provisioned schema is migrated to the tenant-partitioned pack lifecycle, so no runtime login can read or write pack_lifecycle. Every lifecycle entrypoint (compose_reference_stores, DurableGovernedEducationPacks, configuration, and the E/H/P fixture builders) defaults to partitioned and refuses partitioned_lifecycle=False before any I/O. The recovered regulated composition, an alternate route naming the legacy ledger, fails closed at the database. legacy_lifecycle=True provisioning remains only as migration evidence (test_lifecycle_migration, the legacy contract test). Single-login durability fixtures (test_durable_governance, test_pack_delivery, test_governed_packs) bind the recovered ledger directly in the test; product code refuses it. Composition tests formerly parametrised ordinary/partitioned now run partitioned only, so their collected test count is lower.

Two keyed governed pins: exactly fixture-retry-pin-school-a/-b, requests pin(school-a)/pin(school-b), held only in the governing tenant's forced-RLS scope; installation retries empty; index exactly 2 digests. The installation store holds only tenant-less receipts by construction, and every lawful governed operation carries its governance receipt.

The profile's RLS tables (35: the contract's 34 incl. rosters and governed receipts, plus reference_pack_tenants_v1) are seeded for two tenants and pinned field for field. Reads, the 26 INSERT grants and all column UPDATE grants are exercised.

EgressGovernanceTarget refuses a duplicate send at egress inside the recovered target's own paths (verifier C060-PRE-R2). A stored COMMITTED or UNKNOWN replay, before or after a lost claim, raises DuplicateSendRefused, and so does losing the nonce claim to an earlier or concurrent holder. Nothing is sent, spent or recorded. A permit whose earlier delivery was refused still answers FAILED: nothing is sent, and its held budget can settle. The outcome of a dispatched permit stays observable only through reconcile and the bound receipt. Tests cover the replay after commit, the replay after a lost acknowledgement and reconcile, the managed-host path, and a send that loses the claim to another holder (public permit-use store).

A bare filesystem target (no session admission, no database decision-age bound) receives a permit valid in every respect except its absolute expiry. It is refused by require_permit_clock alone, with a pre-expiry verify control. Author pre-check only, not evidence: with A19-4 removed this test fails.

changes.id: durable governed qualification and issuer registries
changes.note: qualification_target and issuer_target now commit through PostgreSQL registries under the mandatory budget. One transaction under the subject's advisory lock: approved-prior check, then the budget final check on that connection, then the append and the governing tenant's receipt (forced RLS). Commit once; replay applies nothing; a failure after the final check rolls back effect, receipt and consumption and stays UNKNOWN; a lost acknowledgement is resolved by the receipt. The in-memory registries remain refused. MATRIX governance-targets open item resolved.

scope_justification_registries: reference_qualification_reports_v1 and reference_issuer_recognitions_v1 are classified installation authority (HOST_METADATA), not tenant RLS tables, because their rows carry no tenant content. A qualification report attests a verifier class against a dataset, signed by the qualification authority; an issuer recognition binds a trust-anchored key to a credential kind. Both are read by every tenant's host, as the in-memory registries were. The only tenant-bearing fields of a governed change (tenant, operation, nonce, change digest) are written to reference_governed_receipts_v1, which is under forced RLS and pinned in POLICIES.json. Grants: governor SELECT/INSERT on all three; receiver SELECT on the two registries only. verifier's review of this scope is pending; it is not claimed as accepted.
